title: Your 2021-22 Smart Classroom Management Report Card port-card/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin presents a fifteen-item, self-graded report card for teachers to assess their own classroom management performance at the close of the school year, covering areas like consistency, calm enforcement of consequences, avoidance of intimidation, worthy praise, and personal wellbeing. He frames the exercise as valuable because it provides objective clarity and self-awareness that's hard to access in the moment during the school year. Beyond the checklist itself, the article recommends a concrete follow-up: listing areas most in need of improvement, breaking them into small actionable steps, and reviewing that plan periodically over the summer before recommitting just before the new year begins. He points readers to the site's archive and search tools for guidance on specific weak areas identified through the exercise. The piece closes with a call to make a genuine promise to oneself to follow through on the identified improvements.
points: A fifteen-item self-graded report card lets teachers assess their year across consistency, calm consequence enforcement, praise practices, and personal wellbeing.
The stated purpose of grading yourself is to gain objective clarity and self-awareness that's difficult to access during the busy school year itself.
Teachers are advised to turn weak areas from the report card into a written, itemized improvement plan rather than leaving the reflection abstract.
Improvement steps should be broken down as small and simple as possible, then reviewed periodically over the summer.
The exercise is meant to culminate in a genuine personal commitment, reviewed again just before the new school year, to follow through on the identified changes.
quotes: Grading yourself post school year enables you to view your classroom management performance objectively.
It allows you to hone in on your weaknesses and reflect on how they can become strengths.
I enforced consequences calmly and objectively (like a referee) ____
I recommend making a list of areas in most need of improvement. Jot down a heading of each on their own separate sheet of paper or Word document.
Break down your steps as small and simple as possible. Review them periodically over the summer , and then just prior to the new year, commit to following them.
Make a promise to yourself, come what may, and you’ll be a better, stronger teacher next year.
